statement: Every actual order-four full torus representative has a unique nonzero invariant mod-two character, and every labelled cusp-normalizer root has nonzero value under its extension killing the order-four section. An explicit discrete cusp-preserving basis makes the actual double-cover homology matrix completely determined by the base matrix and the multiplier. The closed normal subgroup generated by x^2 and (xy)^2 is invariant. Its full quotient is exactly Zhat semidirect C2, with x the reflection, y the rotation, and c the negative second power of the rotation. The induced automorphism has exact order two and the explicit formulas r to r^(-lambda), t to r^j t, with j_2 odd and (1-lambda)j=0. Thus every remaining negative quartic coordinate gives an actual nonabelian dihedral quotient fixed pointwise by the representative.
depends_on: D46 actual order-four representative; D55 positive-square minus-identity homology at every prime, global square multiplier, and primary cusp-normalizer unit; actual discrete double cover and Schreier basis; the inverse quotient presentation maps and integral matrix calculations proved here
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Both directions of the basis and quotient presentation maps are explicit. The original cusp remains c=[x,y] and has the exact image r^(-2). The cover's boundary line and handle lattice are compared by the actual inclusion matrix, without an integral direct-sum assumption at two.
notes: On the rank-three double-cover module the cusp-normalizer action T commutes with the deck involution J and satisfies T^2=-J. Its two-primary fourth norm is exactly 2(I-J), whose boundary image contains only even multiples. The unit cusp exponent forces the root's odd character label, giving the actual section action S=JT. Its anti-deck character supplies the full invariant quotient and all finite dihedral maps. The quotient action has order two even though the original representative has order four. These equations constrain actual actions; they do not realize or exclude the remaining scalar quartic signs, and they do not infer full section generation from the finite quotient.
computational_checks: code/part_c/torus_quartic_dihedral_d68.py and adjacent output/stdout verify free-word basis and cusp identities, exact double-cover matrices and norms, the geometric quartic control, and the finite primary dihedral formulas.
